newsitem.title: THAILAND: Chavalit says new Thai coalition united, advancing.
newsitem.headline: Chavalit says new Thai coalition united, advancing.

text.p: Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, the man set to be Thailand's next premier, on Wednesday dismissed talk of friction within his six-party coalition and said it was working together to quickly form a new cabinet.
Chavalit, whose New Aspiration Party (NAP) won the most seats in Sunday's general election, held a news conference with the leaders of the five other parties in the coalition to show their unity.

Earlier, NAP and the second-largest coalition partner, the Chart Pattana Party, had disagreed over the role to be played by Amnuay Viravan -- a respected economist and banker -- in the future government, coalition sources said.
Chavalit had wanted to give Amnuay, who did not run in the election, the finance minister's job and free rein to manage economic portfolios, the sources said.
But Chart Pattana, led by former prime minister Chatichai Choonhavan, disagreed and said it wanted its own members to have some say in key economic posts.

Although Amnuay was still likely to become finance minister and deputy prime minister in charge of the economy, he would not have complete control over all economic ministries and would not likely bring in a team of outsiders as he had planned, coalition sources and analysts said.
"I have said many times that Amnuay will lead the economic team and I stand by that," Chavalit told Reuters before the news conference.
Amnuay, who was finance minister in 1980-81, did not attend the meeting of coalition partners on Wednesday. But he said earlier in the day he would agree to the new job description.

"I am willing to accept the position of deputy prime minister and also resuming the finance portfolio, and I have no pre-condition about working with elected MPs," Amnuay said after returning from an economic meeting in Hong Kong.
In Hong Kong, Amnuay had said he wanted to approve members of the economic team and to direct economic policy.
A senior member of the Chart Pattana party told Reuters that they want to oversee some economic ministries such as commerce, industry, and transport and communication.
"To my knowledge, the (NAP) has already softened their stance and agreed to have our party share responsibilities in those ministries," a senior Chart Pattana source told Reuters.

Chavalit told the news conference that the NAP and other coalition partners -- Chart Pattana, Social Action Party, Prachakorn Thai, Seritham and Muon Chon -- were working as fast as possible to form policies for the new administration.
"Tomorrow, we will sit down (and) begin to write our policies by merging those of each party to make a unified policy," he said.
He said his coalition was awaiting a royal degree calling the first sitting of parliament.

After parliament resumes, the parties will choose the president of the parliament who will then present the nomination for prime minister -- most likely Chavalit -- to King Bhumibol Adulyadej for his approval.
"We are racing against time, but we must follow the procedures step by step," Chavalit said.
Traditionally, it takes about two weeks from the election before the new government assumes power.
